name: The demonic endowment
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: The demonic endowment — hypocrisy, arrogance, excessive pride, anger, harshness and ignorance (16.4) — leads to bondage (16.5); its bearers know neither engaging nor refraining, hold that the world is without truth, foundation or Lord and caused by desire, are driven by insatiable desire and anxiety, boast, sacrifice in name only, hate the Lord in all bodies, fall into hell and are cast into demonic wombs (16.7–20).
antidotes: giving up desire, anger and greed (16.21–22)
acting by the ordinance of scripture (16.24)

name: The three gates of hell: desire, anger, greed
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Desire, anger and greed are the threefold gate of hell, destructive of the self; one freed from these three gates of darkness does what is good for himself and goes to the highest goal (16.21–22).

name: Hypocrisy of the unrealised (dambha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Hypocrisy/ostentation: first mark of the demonic endowment (16.4); it makes sacrifice and austerity rājasic (17.12, 17.18) and, with egoism, makes unscriptural austerity demonic (17.5).

name: Lack of faith (aśraddhā)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Want of faith: sacrifice without faith is tāmasic (17.13); whatever is offered, given, practised or done without faith is 'asat', of no worth here or hereafter (17.28).

name: The sense of 'I am the doer' (kartṛtva-abhimāna)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: One who, from unrefined understanding, sees the self alone as the doer does not see (18.16); the one whose state is not ego-made is not bound (18.17).
antidotes: seeing the five causes of action (18.13–15)

name: Attachment to the fruits of action; making the fruit one's motive (karmaphala-hetu)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Action, sacrifice, giving and steadfastness aimed at the fruit are rājasic (17.12, 17.21, 18.27, 18.34); the threefold fruit of action comes after death to those who have not relinquished (18.12).

name: The sense of 'I' (ahaṃkāra)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Ego ('I'-making): resorted to by the demonic (16.18); with it action is rājasic (18.24) and austerity demonic (17.5); out of it Arjuna might not listen and perish (18.58) or resolve not to fight, vainly (18.59); cast off by the one fit for becoming brahman (18.53).

name: Delusion (moha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Delusion: giving up prescribed action from it is tāmasic (18.7); action undertaken through it is tāmasic (18.25); through it Arjuna does not want to do what his nature will compel (18.60); its destruction is the stated result of the teaching (18.72–73).

name: Cavilling (asūyā)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Cavilling: the teaching is not to be told to one who cavils at Kṛṣṇa (18.67); hearing it without cavilling is fruitful (18.71); the demonic are cavillers (16.18).

name: Arrogance (stabdhatā)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Stubbornness/arrogance: the demonic are stubborn (16.17); the tāmasic doer is stubborn (18.28).

name: Laziness (ālasya)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Sloth: the tāmasic doer is lazy (18.28); tāmasic happiness arises from sleep, sloth and heedlessness (18.39).

name: Bondage by the three guṇas
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: No being on earth or among the gods is free from the three guṇas born of prakṛti (18.40).
